description: Multi-step tool-calling tasks chaining real OSHA enforcement data with real eCFR regulatory text. Scored deterministically (grounded-citation check), not by an LLM judge — the metrics that matter are tokens/cost/tool-calls/latency to a correct, grounded answer, since that's what an 'efficiency' claim between models should show up in.

test_cases.name: Most-cited fall protection standard for commercial building construction
test_cases.goal: For NAICS code 236220 (commercial building construction), look at OSHA inspections opened between 2023-01-01 and 2023-12-31. Identify the most frequently cited OSHA standard among those inspections, then fetch the actual regulatory text of that standard from 29 CFR Part 1926 (use as_of_date 2023-12-31) and tell me, in one sentence, what it requires. Give your final answer as: 'The most-cited standard is <CFR citation, e.g. 1926.501>: <one-sentence summary of the requirement>.'

test_cases.name: Scaffold violation standard lookup
test_cases.goal: For NAICS code 238910 (site preparation contractors), look at OSHA inspections opened between 2022-06-01 and 2022-12-31. Find the most frequently cited standard related to scaffolding, then fetch its text from 29 CFR Part 1926 (as_of_date 2022-12-31) and summarize the core requirement in one sentence. Final answer format: 'The most-cited scaffolding standard is <CFR citation>: <summary>.'

test_cases.name: Excavation hazard standard lookup
test_cases.goal: For NAICS code 237310 (highway, street, and bridge construction), look at OSHA inspections opened between 2023-01-01 and 2023-06-30. Find the most frequently cited standard related to excavations, then fetch its text from 29 CFR Part 1926 (as_of_date 2023-06-30) and summarize the core requirement in one sentence. Final answer format: 'The most-cited excavation standard is <CFR citation>: <summary>.'
